message.content:
Painting the Eiffel Tower from scratch would be a massive undertaking—think of a 324‑meter‑tall lattice structure with thousands of steel beams, rivets, and exposed surfaces. Even though the tower is routinely repainted every 7–10 years (to protect against rust), a full repaint from the ground up would involve:

| Task | Rough Time Estimate |
|------|---------------------|
| **Preparation** (cleaning, rust removal, surface prep) | 1–2 weeks |
| **Primer application** (protective base coat) | 1–2 weeks |
| **Top‑coat layers** (actual paint) | 2–3 weeks |
| **Detail work** (painting railings, decorative elements, signage) | 1–2 weeks |
| **Drying & curing** (allow paint to set properly) | 1–2 weeks |
| **Inspection & touch‑ups** | 1 week |

Adding all that together, you’re looking at roughly **8–12 weeks** (about 2–3 months) of continuous work, assuming a dedicated crew, optimal weather, and no major interruptions. In practice, the actual schedule could stretch longer due to logistical constraints, safety protocols, and the need to keep the tower open to visitors.

If you’re asking about how long it takes to paint a single section or a small part of the tower, that would be much less—perhaps a few days for a small crew. But for a full, comprehensive repaint of the entire structure, expect a couple of months of coordinated effort.
